On 2026-11-20 the user asked to "work on a1+ Unit 7 same all deal as before none stop all approved": the A1+ Unit 7 map (A1+ 7.Y follows A1 7.Y, one step each, fifteen lessons) approved up front, straight to Preview, Gemini 2.5 Flash photos and ElevenLabs audio pre-approved, no per-lesson gates, reviewed in Preview. Four new photos (Gemini 2.5 Flash): Sofia presses her forehead, Luis rubs his bare feet on a park bench, Diego holds his legs after a run, Ana presses her closed eyes at a bright laptop. Each photo shows one body part hurting, so a picture bank tells head, feet, legs and eyes apart; the person who hurts says the first-person line.

lesson.title: 7.1 What's wrong? My head hurts
lesson.unit_title: Everyday needs, plans and free time
lesson.unit_outcome: Say what hurts and why someone feels a certain way, describe what people are wearing and the weather as it happens, tell someone to put on or take off clothes, talk about what people like doing, invite and answer, ask someone to repeat or explain, talk about being sick, the months and seasons, compare with the biggest and the tallest, and say what people and animals can do and are good at.
lesson.goal: Say what hurts with hurts and hurt (My head hurts. / My feet hurt.) and ask What's wrong?.
lesson.grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 7.1 My Body: A1 names the body (This is my head. I have two feet.); A1+ 7.1 says what hurts. The one new grammar relationship is a body part + hurts or hurt: one thing takes hurts (My head hurts.) and two take hurt (My feet hurt. / My legs hurt. / My eyes hurt.), with my, his and her before the body part; the question is What's wrong?. Four new photos show the cast in pain: Sofia's head, Luis's feet after a walk, Diego's legs after a run and Ana's eyes at a bright screen, and A1 7.2's tired and sad come back in front of the reason (I'm tired and my legs hurt.).
lesson.prerequisite: A1 7.1 the body; A1 7.2 How are you? tired and sad; A1 3.10 his and her; A1+ 3.4 short forms of be.
lesson.speaking_outcome: Say hurts with a clear s (HURTS) after head, and hurt with no s after feet, legs and eyes; say What's wrong? as two words (WHATS-RONG). Do not require native-like speed.
